newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TVS Suzuki sees turnover rise.
newsitem.headline: India's TVS Suzuki sees turnover rise.

text.p: Indian motorcycle and scooter maker TVS Suzuki Ltd said on Wednesday that it expects turnover to rise by 37 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) and plans to invest more than three billion rupees by 2000.

"The company plans to invest nearly three billion rupees by the year 2000 to expand its existing facilities and to set up a scooter project," vice president R.L. Ravichandran told Reuters following a news conference in the Indian capital.
India's TVS group has a 30 percent stake in TVS Suzuki while Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp owns 26 percent. The rest is held by the public.
TVS Suzuki expects turnover to rise to 8.5 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 6.22 billion recorded last year, Ravichandran said.
Ravichandran said the company had earmarked 1.5 billion rupees for its planned plant in the southern city of Mysore.
"A major chunk of the investment would be taken by our new plant in Mysore where we plan to manufacture 250,000 scooters annually," he said.
Karnataka state had already approved the plant, which Ravichandran said would be operational by April 1998.
TVS Suzuki has an 18 percent share of India's two-wheeler market which includes motorcycles, mopeds and small 70 cc scooters. It does not make the more popular 125 cc scooters.
Bajaj Auto is the market leader in the 125 cc scooter segment, accounting for almost 69 percent of the 1.22 million unit scooter market in 1995/96.
Ravichandran said with its new plant, TVS Suzuki hopes to raise its share of the two-wheeler market to 25 percent.
Analysts say the scooter market is growing at an annual rate of 18 percent.
Over the two financial years 1995/96 and 1996/97, TVS Suzuki invested 800 million rupees to expand the capacity of its Hosur plant in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
"We are increasing the capacity of our Hosur plant from the existing 400,000 units to 600,000 units a year," Ravichandran said.
The Hosur plant manufactures motorcycles, mopeds and small scooters.
